name: Storm-1295
iocPatterns: Malicious domains used in phishing campaigns
Spear-phishing with custom URLs leading to credential theft
keyCapabilities: Synchronous relay servers for creating replica sign-in pages
recommendedActions: Enhance email filtering to detect malicious links
Conduct regular user training on phishing awareness
Monitor for domain name system (DNS) tunneling activities
Regularly update and patch software vulnerabilities
campaignsText: Storm-1295's campaigns typically involve mass phishing attempts, leveraging their platform to distribute malicious links and payloads. Their operational tempo is moderate but effective due to their service-based model. Microsoft tracking indicates they have been active since mid-2022, with notable campaigns including those targeting financial institutions and healthcare sectors.
description: Storm-1295, also known as DEV-1295, is a threat actor group operating since mid-2022 that provides phishing-as-a-service through the Greatness platform. They specialize in creating replica sign-in pages using synchronous relay servers to steal credentials and offer their services to other attackers. Their activities are tracked by Microsoft, highlighting their potential impact on various sectors.
goals: Storm-1295 primarily targets sectors with valuable data or financial interests due to the nature of their phishing campaigns. Their strategic objective appears to be profit-driven, catering to other attackers by providing ready-to-use phishing tools. This makes them a significant threat to organizations across various industries, as they can facilitate large-scale credential theft and potential ransomware deployments.
